solution.concept_anchor: Nationally designated reserves not in UNESCO MAB — Cold Desert and Dibru-Saikhowa

statement_analysis.statement: Both Cold Desert (Himachal Pradesh) and Dibru-Saikhowa (Assam) are nationally designated biosphere reserves that have not yet been included in the UNESCO MAB network.
statement_analysis.reason: Cold Desert and Dibru-Saikhowa are both among the six nationally designated Indian biosphere reserves that remain outside the UNESCO MAB network — this is a documented and testable fact.

statement_analysis.statement: Cold Desert Biosphere Reserve supports snow leopard populations but no significant human settlements, as its extreme altitude and cold conditions make permanent habitation impossible.
statement_analysis.reason: Cold Desert does host human settlements — Kibber (Spiti, Himachal Pradesh) is one of the world's highest inhabited villages, and communities live in Pin Valley, Kaza, and other areas within or adjacent to the reserve's transition zone. Permanent habitation is not 'impossible' — it is a documented feature of the reserve.

statement_analysis.statement: Dibru-Saikhowa Biosphere Reserve is situated in the upper Brahmaputra floodplain and is known for its semi-wild horse population inhabiting the riverine islands.
statement_analysis.reason: Dibru-Saikhowa occupies the upper Brahmaputra floodplain in Tinsukia and Dibrugarh districts; its defining ecological feature is the feral (semi-wild) horse population on the chapori (floodplain island) grasslands.

solution.strong_distractor: d — Students who have memorised Cold Desert's extreme climate may accept Statement 2's 'impossible to inhabit' claim without recalling Kibber or Spiti's human settlements.
elimination_logic: Evaluate Statement 1: Cold Desert and Dibru-Saikhowa are both nationally designated but not UNESCO MAB — confirmed; Statement 1 correct.
Evaluate Statement 2: Cold Desert has human settlements (Kibber, Kaza, Pin Valley) — 'no significant human settlements' and 'impossible' are factually wrong; Statement 2 incorrect.
Evaluate Statement 3: Dibru-Saikhowa, upper Brahmaputra floodplain, semi-wild horses — all confirmed; Statement 3 correct.
Statements 1 and 3 correct, Statement 2 incorrect → answer is (b).
solution.upsc_trap_explanation: Statement 2 exploits the assumed inhospitability of high-altitude cold deserts. Students who associate Ladakh/Spiti with extreme remoteness may accept 'no human settlements' as true without recalling that Kibber village and Kaza town (Spiti headquarters) are within the Cold Desert reserve's zone. The scope-extension marker is 'impossible' — a word that should always trigger scrutiny in UPSC multi-statement questions.
solution.final_explanation:
Six of India's 18 nationally designated biosphere reserves remain outside the UNESCO MAB network — of these, Cold Desert and Dibru-Saikhowa are the most frequently examined.

• Statement 1 — Correct: Both Cold Desert and Dibru-Saikhowa are nationally designated reserves that have not been submitted or accepted into the UNESCO MAB Programme. This is the critical factual distinction.
• Statement 2 — Incorrect: Cold Desert does support human communities. Kibber in Spiti Valley is documented as one of the world's highest permanently inhabited villages. The Spiti and Lahaul valleys within the reserve's ambit have settled populations practising traditional livelihoods including agropastoralism. 'Impossible to inhabit' is factually wrong.
• Statement 3 — Correct: Dibru-Saikhowa's feral horse population on its riverine grassland islands (chaporis) is its most distinctive ecological feature, resulting from domesticated horses reverting to a semi-wild state.

Value Addition:
• The Cold Desert reserve spans Pin Valley, Chandratal lake, Sarchu, and Kibber — a diverse trans-Himalayan landscape.
• The Tibetan antelope (chiru) and Tibetan wolf are trans-boundary species present in Cold Desert.
• India has 18 − 12 = 6 nationally designated reserves not in UNESCO MAB; being able to name at least three is an exam asset.

solution.upsc_trap_explanation: 2009 का समूह एक प्रसिद्ध समूह है: नोक्रेक + पचमढ़ी + सिमलीपाल। अचनाकमार-अमरकंटक (जिसे 2012 में यूनेस्को MAB मान्यता मिली — तीन वर्ष बाद) को जोड़ना यह जांचता है कि छात्र सही समूह संरचना जानते हैं या नहीं। मध्य भारत / मध्य प्रदेश का संबंध पचमढ़ी और अचनाकमार-अमरकंटक के बीच जोड़ी को स्वाभाविक बनाता है — दोनों सतपुड़ा-मैकाल क्षेत्र में हैं — लेकिन वर्ष अलग है।
solution.final_explanation:
2009 का यूनेस्को MAB मान्यता समूह भारत के सबसे बड़े समूहों में से एक है — उस वर्ष तीन रिजर्वों को मान्यता मिली।

• जोड़ी 1 (नोक्रेक, 2009) — सही: मेघालय के गारो हिल्स में साइट्रस जीन अभयारण्य; सही वर्ष 2009 में।
• जोड़ी 2 (पचमढ़ी, 2009) — सही: मध्य प्रदेश के सतपुड़ा श्रृंखला का रिजर्व; सही 2009 समूह में।
• जोड़ी 3 (सिमलीपाल, 2009) — सही: ओडिशा के मयूरभंज जिले का साल वन रिजर्व; सही 2009 में।
• जोड़ी 4 (अचनाकमार-अमरकंटक, 2009) — गलत: इस रिजर्व को 2009 में नहीं बल्कि 2012 में यूनेस्को MAB मान्यता मिली। यह 2009 समूह के बाद के चक्र में आता है।

तीन जोड़ी सही मेल खाती हैं।

मूल्यवर्धन:
• याद रखने के लिए यूनेस्को MAB मान्यता वर्ष: 2000 (निलगिरी), 2001 (मन्नार की खाड़ी, सुंदरबन, मानस), 2004 (नंदा देवी), 2009 (नोक्रेक, पचमढ़ी, सिमलीपाल), 2012 (अचनाकमार-अमरकंटक), 2013 (ग्रेट निकोबार), 2016 (अगस्थ्यमलाई), 2018 (खांगचेंदजोंगा)।
• 2001 का समूह भी बड़ा वर्ष है — तीन रिजर्व एक साथ मान्यता प्राप्त।
• अचनाकमार-अमरकंटक की 2012 की मान्यता 2009 समूह से 3 वर्ष बाद आई — यह समय संबंधी भेद है जिसका UPSC ने उपयोग किया है।
